### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dfbe34d8874326be643042c36211ba6ec5e69c7f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `56f21c7480710d3536df4a02f62f50d852d1694d` — the merge of head `0b17ca15d13017ee0fa2303909d430cd3ef43f36` into base `dfbe34d8874326be643042c36211ba6ec5e69c7f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 56f21c7480710d3536df4a02f62f50d852d1694d && git checkout 56f21c7480710d3536df4a02f62f50d852d1694d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin dfbe34d8874326be643042c36211ba6ec5e69c7f 0b17ca15d13017ee0fa2303909d430cd3ef43f36 && git checkout -B drift-repro dfbe34d8874326be643042c36211ba6ec5e69c7f && git merge --no-ff 0b17ca15d13017ee0fa2303909d430cd3ef43f36

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dfbe34d8874326be643042c36211ba6ec5e69c7f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0b17ca15d13017ee0fa2303909d430cd3ef43f36`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/conversions/refused-shapes.ts + packages/spec/src/ui/duplicate-global-filter-names.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts (the `globalFilters` refinement), packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.ui-dashboard-global-filter-duplicate-name-refused.ts (the D3 entry the id names), packages/spec/src/conversions/stored.ts + walk.ts + apply.ts (the sink the detector reports through), packages/spec/src/conversions/refused-shapes.test.ts (the roster pin and the three listing cases), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts `saveMetaItemUnaudited` and packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-diagnostics.ts `computeMetadataDiagnostics` (the save-door and load claims the reason text makes), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.dashboard-duplicate-global-filter-name-refusal.test.ts (the door pin). The remainder of the diff (`.changeset/29212-dashboard-duplicate-filter-stored-listing.md`, `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT.

Inputs read: card #29212 body and its three comments (triage 6574212312, claim 6576712044, os-dev-report 6579168801); PR #29399 body, file list (5 files) and the net diff `57cde8cb...0b17ca15` (+222/−1); the check-runs on `0b17ca15`. Tree read with `git show 0b17ca15:<path>`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged — right.** The diff adds no schema, key, value or refinement. `DashboardSchema.globalFilters`'s `superRefine(refuseDuplicateGlobalFilterNames)` and the predicate module are untouched (sibling #29213's surface, honoured). Every door (`defineStack`, `os validate`, `os build`, save door) accepts and refuses exactly what it did on `main`.
- **Public surface: `REFUSED_STORED_SHAPES` gains one entry — right.** The exported roster grows by `dashboardDuplicateGlobalFilterName`; no new export, so `check:api-surface` has nothing to move and the spec `check:generated` artifacts are unchanged. The only observable change is behavioural: `applyConversionsToStoredItem('dashboard', row, { onTodo })` now hands one `ConversionTodoNotice` per repeated key, `conversionId: 'ui-dashboard-global-filter-duplicate-name-refused'`, which `os migrate meta --stored` prints under the row. On `main` the same row handed zero TODOs (premise re-measured by the dev on `5a2bdf9c`; consistent with the roster on `main`, which registers `objectDuplicateActionName` and no dashboard detector).
- **Registration against the chain — right.** `toMajor: 18` and the id match the step-18 D3 entry `18.ui-dashboard-global-filter-duplicate-name-refused.ts` (landed by #29162, merged as `38a278b7`); the roster pin in `refused-shapes.test.ts` requires each id to be a semantic entry of its step and not a conversion id, and the pinned roster list names the new id last, in report order.
- **Door pin (test-only, `packages/metadata-protocol`) — right.** The new test is the object sibling's harness (`protocol.object-duplicate-action-name-refusal.test.ts`) with the dashboard body, widened to the three modes. `saveMetaItemUnaudited` runs the per-type Zod parse before any write in draft and publish alike (the gate comment at the `INVALID_METADATA` refusal says the two modes answer the same), and `getMetadataTypeSchema('dashboard')` is `DashboardSchema` (`kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts`), so the 422 at `globalFilters.1.name` with `rows.size === 0` is what the code does, not only what the test says.
- **Ledger (`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`) — right, and the claim covers it.** A new engine double in a test file is exactly what `check-engine-double-contract.mjs --write` records (three rows: `delete`, `findOne`, `update`), and the claim comment's file surface reads "any ledger/listing a gate names". Not reviewed here beyond that.
- **Check-runs on `0b17ca15`** (the gate verdicts): all 64 completed by 2026-11-02T14:29Z — 55 `success`, 9 `skipped` (opt-in and path-gated jobs: UI Published Artifacts, Temporal Conformance, Schedule gate, Packed-tarball smoke, Lint UI, Dogfood Verify CLI, Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Build Docs, 18.x upgrade harness), 0 `failure`. Green among them: Test Core (8/8 shards), Type Check · source gates / debt ledger / workspace / consumer gates / UI, Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Test UI (16/16), every Lint family, Spec property liveness, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Dogfood Regression Gate. The derived gate families answer green; nothing was re-run here.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/29212-dashboard-duplicate-filter-stored-listing.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, body carries `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`; the PR body carries the same two lines. **Right.** Nothing an author can write changes (`none`), the accept set is neither widened nor narrowed (`no`, no arm), so the kind is `none` and the level is `patch` on the one released package the diff moves. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` gains a test file only, so it owes no changeset; `scripts/` publishes nothing. `Check Changeset` on the head is green, and the dev's offline `check-changeset-no-major --event` read `no`/`none` at `patch`.
- No BREAKING banner, no ADR-0087 disposition marker owed (not a narrowing); the entry this detector names was registered by #29023's changeset, which is still in `.changeset/` on the head (unreleased).
- Clause-②: no

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviation 1 — `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` off the named surface.** Answered: inside the claim ("any ledger/listing a gate names"), written by the gate's own `--write`; accepted, see ①.
- **Dev deviation 2 — PR opened with no assignee or reviewer** (harness forbids the MCP write). Answered: a process note, no design bearing; the seat assigns if it wants to.
- **Dev deviation 3 — one `origin/main` merge (27 commits) before opening.** Answered: the net diff against the merge base is the 5 files above and nothing else; the merge brought no stray hunk.
- **open_questions[0] — should the #29023 D3 entry's `acceptanceCriteria` say `os migrate meta --stored` lists the row?** Answered: **A, yes — add the sentence.** The entry is what the upgrade guide renders and what an operator reads when the TODO id is printed; the object sibling's `acceptanceCriteria` (`18.object-duplicate-action-name-refused.ts`) says "os migrate meta --stored lists each stored object that still repeats a name, under the TODO id …", so a reader comparing the two entries would conclude the dashboard row is not listed. The entry is unreleased (its changeset `29023-dashboard-global-filter-duplicate-name.md` is still pending on the head), so the edit is a prose change under `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, no changeset of its own beyond the one that already names the listing, and no gate reads that sentence (`migrations.test.ts` pins other entries' `acceptanceCriteria`, not this one's). It is a **should-fix carried as a one-sentence follow-up**: the file sat outside the claimed surface, the detector is correct without it, and reopening this head for one sentence costs a re-review; the seat may fold it into this PR instead if it prefers one landing, at the price of a fresh record on the new head.
- **out_of_scope_findings[0] — PR #29370 / card #29213's `reservedDateRangeGlobalFilters` refusal has no stored-row detector either.** Escalation: the seat's follow-up card, not the maintainer's. Verified on GitHub: #29370 is still an open draft, not merged, so there is no predicate on `main` to call and the dev was right not to build ahead of it; file the detector card when #29370 lands, shaped like #29212. The dev's note in the PR body says the same.
- **Check-runs** (①): every run on the head has completed green or skipped; nothing is pending against the landing rule's "every check is green".
- Nothing in this PR needs the maintainer's word: no governed path in the file list, no `!`, no `(narrowing)` arm, no release act.

### ④ Design judgment

`hits`: `packages/spec/src/conversions/refused-shapes.ts`. Judged against the D3 entry it names, the predicate it calls, the parse it must agree with, the sink it reports through, and the operator scenario (an upgrade preview over `sys_metadata` before the release that refuses the row).

- **One predicate, two doors — holds.** The detector calls `duplicateGlobalFilterNames(dashboard.globalFilters)`, the same function `refuseDuplicateGlobalFilterNames` feeds `ctx.addIssue` from in `dashboard.zod.ts`; no logic is copied, so the listing and the parse refuse one set by construction. I tried to split them: (a) `GlobalFilterSchema.name` is `z.string().optional()` with no `.default()`, so the array the parse's `superRefine` sees carries `name` exactly where the stored row does and the `field` fallback resolves the same on both sides (the test's three-entry `field` case pins it: parse at `['globalFilters', 1, 'field']`, listing at `dashboards[0].globalFilters[1].field`, indexes `[0, 1, 2]`); (b) `strictObject` `aliases` (`key → name`, `fieldName → field`) are refusal prescriptions from the `unrecognized_keys` path, never accepted spellings, so a stored row cannot hold a `key:` the parse would read as `name` and the detector would not; (c) a non-array or absent `globalFilters` yields `[]` from the predicate and `mapCollection` skips non-dict rows, so no stored dashboard crashes the pass. No split found.
- **The site is the parse's site — holds.** `path` is `${path}.globalFilters[${indexes[1]}].${secondKey}`, the second declaration's `name` or `field`, which is the issue path the refinement emits (`[indexes[1], secondKey]` under `globalFilters`). The object sibling reports `actions[1]` because its parse refuses at the entry; this one reports one key deeper because its parse does. Correct, and pinned in both directions.
- **Reaches the operator — holds.** `applyConversionsToStoredItem('dashboard', …)` maps `dashboard → dashboards` through `SINGULAR_TO_PLURAL` (`metadata-collection.zod.ts`), so `mapCollection(stack, 'dashboards', …)` sees the row; `applyConversions` runs `reportRefusedStoredShapes` only under an `onTodo` sink, and builds the notice with `conversionId: refused.id` and the `[protocol] left … as stored — protocol 18 refuses it (ADR-0087 D3 entry '…')` message, so the TODO carries the upgrade-guide id. Reads only: `detect` returns the dashboard unchanged and the test pins `item` deep-equal to the row.
- **The reason tells the truth about the row's fate — holds.** "still loads with `_diagnostics` reading `valid: false`": `computeMetadataDiagnostics` re-parses a served `dashboard` with `DashboardSchema` and returns `{ valid: false, errors }` on failure, the row is served. "its next save, draft or publish, is refused with 422 INVALID_METADATA": the save door parses before writing in both modes, and the new door test pins all three mode spellings with `rows.size === 0`. The reason ends with the predicate's own message (key, every index, the fix), leads with why nothing rewrites it (which definition keeps the key, and which `filterBindings` meant it, only the author knows), and carries no tracker number (pinned `not.toMatch(/#\d{3,}/)`). `from` carries `{ name, indexes }` only, as the sibling does; a filter body carries no secret, but the shape is uniform.
- **Scenario check.** Blast radius measured on the card body: 0 authored dashboards repeat a key, so this is a guard. An operator running `os migrate meta --stored` before upgrading to the release that carries #29023 now sees each affected `sys_metadata` dashboard, by name and index, instead of a silent `valid: false` after the upgrade. The dev's ablation (deleting the registry line reds the roster pin and both listing cases, the control stays green) shows the three new cases bite on the registration, not only on the predicate.
- **Findings.** Must-fix: none. Should-fix (not in the `hits` file, carried as a follow-up): the D3 entry's `acceptanceCriteria` should say the row is listed under this TODO id (③, open_questions[0]). Nothing else: `surface` wording differs from the entry's `surface` by an "of one dashboard" clause, as the object sibling's does from its entry, and no gate or reader compares the two.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：`os migrate meta --stored` 现在会列出「同一个看板里两个全局筛选器用了同一个 key」的已存数据行。另加一个测试，钉住保存接口在三种模式下都拒收这种看板。
- 为什么改：#29023 已经让保存接口拒收这种看板，但升级前的存量预览不报它，运维在升级前看不到哪些看板下次保存会被拒。
- 风险与回滚：只加了只读检测和测试，任何入口的接受/拒收结果都不变。回滚就是 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/spec/src/conversions/refused-shapes.ts`（新 detector，调用与解析同一个判定函数）。

- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

席位意见：可落地。契约复审在现 head 判 PASS，CI 全绿。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · `domain:spec#2` · head `0b17ca15`

1. **Shape:** draft, base `main`, `Fixes #29212`. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` sit at line start in the body and the changeset (`@objectstack/spec` patch). There are 5 files, +222/−1. The surface is `refused-shapes.ts`, its test, a new `metadata-protocol` test file and the changeset, all inside claim 6576712044. The gate-written `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` (3 rows) is declared as a deviation. No governed path.
2. **Premise measured:** on `5a2bdf9c`, a stored dashboard with two filters named `r` gave 0 TODOs from `--stored`, while the object control gave 1. On the head the new detector `dashboardDuplicateGlobalFilterName` (TODO id `ui-dashboard-global-filter-duplicate-name-refused`) lists it at `dashboards[i].globalFilters[j].name` (or `.field`), the same site the parse refuses. The review confirmed it calls the refinement's own predicate `duplicateGlobalFilterNames` and rewrites nothing.
3. **Gates:** `ci-failure.mjs --sha 0b17ca15…` GREEN: 64 check-runs, none failed, none superseded. The 9 skipped are opt-in or path-gated.
4. **Accepted deviations:** the pinned engine-double rows (written by `--write`, as the gate prescribes), the one `origin/main` merge, and no assignee or reviewer on the PR (the order forbids MCP writes).
5. **Out of scope:** the #29023 D3 entry's `acceptanceCriteria` should say `--stored` lists the row (dev Q1, answered A). It is a one-sentence prose edit to an unreleased entry, so it rides on the follow-up detector card for #29213's `reservedDateRange` refusal, which is filed when PR #29370 lands. The body carries no `Skills-docs:` line; `PR-body guards` passed, and no skill lists `--stored` TODO ids, so nothing is owed.
6. **Landing:** not Tier H and under 3000 lines, so the seat lands it with `pr_ready` and auto-merge. After merge, the seat writes a landing note on #29212 and removes `pm:dispatched`.
